## TL;DR

The macOS Hub CI job was red because `HubFindBarContainerTests.testHidingFindBarReturnsFocusToThePage` crashed XCTest’s memory checker at teardown, not because of a flaky focus assertion. The test now follows the same window lifecycle pattern as other Hub window tests, asserts focus through `containsKeyboardFocus(in:)` (matching production Cmd-F bookkeeping), and waits for `hideFindInterface`’s async first-responder handoff. Swift 6 concurrency warnings in `LocalServerDiscoveryTests` were cleaned up with `OSAllocatedUnfairLock`. Documentation in `docs/macos-hub-release.md` records the root cause and fix.

## Work and rationale

GitHub Actions run 41769376401 (v0.5.75 release, 2026-11-04) shows a single failing test in the **Build and test native Hub** job: `HubFindBarContainerTests.testHidingFindBarReturnsFocusToThePage()`, reported at 0.000 s. Failed-step logs name the test but do not print an `XCTAssert` message. Pulling the xcresult locally shows the real failure mode: **Crash: RepoOS Hub at `-[XCTMemoryChecker _assertInvalidObjectsDeallocatedAfterScope:]`**. That checker runs when a test creates AppKit objects (here a real `WKWebView` inside an `NSWindow`) and tears down without releasing them cleanly. The old test called `window.close()` immediately after a fixed 0.25 s run-loop spin, without `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`, without clearing `contentView`, and without ordering the window out first—unlike `HubWorkspaceChromeTests` and `HubSnapshotSupport`, which explicitly document safe offscreen/window hosting.

The product behavior under test is still valid: when the user closes the Hub find bar after typing in it, keyboard focus should return to the page so Find Next/Previous stay wired correctly (#0789 / #0795). Production code already restores focus in `hideFindInterface()` on the main queue when the bar owned focus. The test fix keeps that contract but measures it the way the app does—`containsKeyboardFocus(in:)` treats the web view, its descendants, and the find field’s shared field editor as “page focus,” rather than requiring `window.firstResponder === webView`, which is brittle with `NSSearchField` editors.

Implementation details in the test: size the container, mark the window `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`, use `defer` to `orderOut`, nil the content view, drain the main run loop briefly, then close; call a small `settleFocusWindow` helper after `makeKeyAndOrderFront` and after `presentFindInterface`; poll until the bar is hidden and `containsKeyboardFocus` is true. Locally the test now passes in ~0.5 s instead of failing instantly.

Separately, CI compile logs showed Swift 6 language-mode **warnings** (not failures) in `LocalServerDiscoveryTests.swift`: mutating a captured `snapshots` array inside `onUpdate`, and `NSLock` from `async` health-check doubles. Those tests were already green on CI. Refactoring to `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` and a `PartialSnapshotRecorder` removes the warnings so strict Swift 6 does not later fail the job. No production discovery code changed.

## Approaches tried

Initial hypothesis from the task text was “headless CI cannot hold keyboard focus.” Local reproduction on a Mac with a GUI disproved that: the same crash reproduced outside CI. Inspecting xcresult diagnostics shifted the fix toward lifecycle/teardown rather than weakening or deleting the test. An intermediate version kept `firstResponder === webView`; switching to `containsKeyboardFocus(in:)` aligns with `HubServerWebContainerView`’s public focus API and avoids fighting AppKit’s field editor.

## Challenges and blockers

GitHub `--log-failed` output for this job does not surface XCTest memory-checker crashes as readable assertion text; xcresult export was required to see the true signature. Full `xcodebuild test` on the engineer machine also showed unrelated `LocalServerDiscoveryTests` failures (empty discovery results), likely from a broken local Xcode/CoreDevice toolchain pairing; those tests pass on CI per run 41769376401. **This session did not re-run the workflow on GitHub** after the fix—CI green on push to main remains for the merge pipeline to confirm.

## Key learnings

A 0.000 s “failed” Hub unit test on CI can be XCTest aborting at scope exit, not an immediate `XCTAssert`. Any Hub test that hosts `WKWebView` in a window should copy the established teardown pattern and assert focus through `containsKeyboardFocus(in:)` when find-bar editors are involved. When macOS Hub CI compile warnings mention Swift 6 concurrency in test doubles, fix them before they become errors even if the test target still passes today.
